answers.core: Yes, as I said there's no good way to address it in a game and it would better to give developers more control and freedom to manually fix the issue themselves the way games have dealt with the problem for a long time, forcibly compile at a load screen. I know this is an ongoing discussion, and 4.4 is great with many improvements that have addressed it for Forward+ rendering, but I am trying to present this as a more unique take on addressing the issue deterministically in the compatibility renderers and such.
answers.workaround:
I don't consider any workaround currently to be viable because the view frustum is not deterministic and hard to get right, many users fail at it and rendering server just doesn't expose a way yet.

A workaround that I am using if you are using the compatibility renderer is to just stick to only a single material type, like the built in one, and not use any shaders. Either that or use a very small limited number of shaders that apply to all/many objects so the number of shader compile invocations is limited. This is basically following your own form of ubershaders to an extent, and that's basically what I'm doing currently.
